question.text: The main scale of a vernier calliper reads <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn></math> divisions. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn></math> divisions of vernier scale coincide with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>9</mn></math> divisions of the main scale. When the two jaws of the callipers touch each other, the fifth division of the vernier coincides with a main scale division and the zero of the vernier is to the right of zero of the main scale. When a cylinder is tightly placed between the two jaws, the zero of vernier scale lies slightly to the left of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mtext>3.2</mtext><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> and the fourth vernier division coincides with a main scale division. The diameter of the cylinder is

solution.text:
Zero error = 0.5 mm = 0.05 cm

observed reading of cylinder = 3.2 cm + (4) (0.01 cm) = 3.24 cm

actual thickness of cylinder = (3.24) – (0.05) = 3.19 cm.
